messages:
lina: quick q — my Go client is getting 401s calling the hosted API. I set Authorization: Basic <base64(apiKey)> but it still fails. anyone seen this?

samir: common trap: Basic expects base64(username:password). if you're using API key as the username and no password, you must include the trailing colon before encoding. e.g. base64('sk-...:')

kevin: yup. also watch how you build the env var. if you do `echo 'sk-xxx' > /tmp/key` and then `cat /tmp/key | base64` you'll get a newline in the value unless you used `echo -n`. that changes the header payload.

maya: concrete examples —
curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n 'sk-ABC123:' | base64)` https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate`

node: `const auth = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(process.env.RW_API_KEY + ':').toString('base64'); fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: auth } })`

python: `import os, base64
api = os.environ.get('RW_API_KEY')
header = 'Basic ' + base64.b64encode((api + ':').encode()).decode()`

go: `api := os.Getenv("RW_API_KEY")
auth := "Basic " + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(api+":"))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", auth)`

samir: another gotcha: some folks accidentally include surrounding quotes in the env var. e.g. export RW_API_KEY="sk-..." -> the value contains the quotes if your runtime reads raw from some config file. always print/debug with something like `printf '%s' "$RW_API_KEY" | xxd` to inspect hidden bytes.

lina: ahhh — I was doing `echo $KEY` and it looked fine but I pasted from a text editor that added CRLF.

kevin: CRLF will break the base64 output if not stripped. on mac/linux use `tr -d '\r'` when cleaning a file. windows powershell: `$env:RW_API_KEY = (Get-Content key.txt -Raw).Trim()`

maya: also note that some HTTP helper libraries let you do `client.SetBasicAuth(user, pass)` which will do the base64 and prefix for you. if you use that, pass the api key as the username and an empty string for password. in Go: `req.SetBasicAuth(apiKey, "")`

samir: small security PSA: avoid printing full api keys in logs. When debugging, base64 encode and compare prefixes, or show lengths.

dev-ex-bot: deploy-bot noticed 3 recent 401s from a CI runner in project/x — tagging @lina for follow-up.

lina: thanks — fixed. turns out my CI secret had a trailing newline; switched to `echo -n` when writing the secret and redeployed. all good :thumbsup:

kevin: awesome. leaving a quick snippet for the wiki: `Authorization` must be `Basic <base64(apiKey:)>` — include the colon even if password is empty. also watch for newlines, CRLF, and accidental quotes in env files.

maya: adding that to devex FAQ now.

lina: fwiw, one more edge: if you base64 in CI step using `echo 'sk-..:' | base64` (no -n), GitHub Actions runners on linux will include newline; use `echo -n` or `printf '%s'`.
